title: A Theory of Marriage: Part I
abstract_level_finding: Foundational model of gains from marriage and equilibrium matching; fertility connection requires later models or empirical tests.

title: The Truly Disadvantaged
abstract_level_finding: Introduces the economic marriageability account for declining marriage among disadvantaged populations; fertility effect requires separate evidence.

authors: Schwartz, Christine R.; Mare, Robert D.
title: Trends in Educational Assortative Marriage from 1940 to 2003
design_or_role: repeated cross-sectional census and CPS analysis
abstract_level_finding: Documents changing educational homogamy; contains no identified fertility effect in the inspected abstract.

title: Marriage Market Mismatches in Japan: An Alternative View of the Relationship between Women's Education and Marriage
design_or_role: decomposition using National Fertility Survey rounds
abstract_level_finding: Tests whether educational composition and matching propensities account for declining marriage; fertility outcome not established in the inspected record.

authors: Greenwood, Jeremy; Guner, Nezih; Kocharkov, Georgi; Santos, Cezar
title: Marry Your Like: Assortative Mating and Income Inequality
abstract_level_finding: Documents educational sorting and studies household inequality, not a fertility effect.

title: Booms, Busts, and Fertility: Testing the Becker Model Using Gender-Specific Labor Demand
abstract_level_finding: Better male labor-market conditions are associated with higher birth rates; better female conditions have smaller negative effects.

title: Male Earnings, Marriageable Men, and Nonmarital Fertility: Evidence from the Fracking Boom
abstract_level_finding: Fracking raised noncollege male earnings and both marital and nonmarital births, with no detected rise in marriage.

authors: Autor, David; Dorn, David; Hanson, Gordon
title: When Work Disappears: Manufacturing Decline and the Falling Marriage Market Value of Young Men
abstract_level_finding: Trade shocks that reduced young men's relative employment and earnings also reduced marriage and fertility.

authors: Charles, Kerwin Kofi; Luoh, Ming Ching
title: Male Incarceration, the Marriage Market, and Female Outcomes
design_or_role: fixed effects and IV using incarceration policy variation
abstract_level_finding: Higher male imprisonment reduced women's marriage and spouse quality; the inspected abstract reports schooling and labor supply rather than fertility.

title: The Impact of Education on Family Formation: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from the UK
abstract_level_finding: The reform reduced teen fertility but not completed fertility and changed spouse education and cohort matching; direct schooling incapacitation remains a competing channel.

title: Women's Schooling and Fertility under Low Female Labor Force Participation: Evidence from Mobility Restrictions in Israel
design_or_role: natural experiment from eased mobility restrictions
abstract_level_finding: Female schooling rose and completed fertility fell; spousal education also rose through assortative matching, but the inspected summary does not establish a formal mediation decomposition.

authors: Silva, José Henrique Costa Monteiro da; Lima, Everton E.; Oliveira, Maria Coleta Ferreira Albino de
title: Educational Pairings and Fertility Decline in Brazil: An Analysis Using Cohort Fertility
abstract_level_finding: Relates changes in educational pairings to the fertility transition; causal selection into unions remains unresolved.

authors: Lichter, Daniel T.; Price, Joseph P.; Swigert, Jeffrey M.
title: Mismatches in the Marriage Market
design_or_role: ACS construction of multidimensional partner shortages
abstract_level_finding: Finds deficits of potential spouses defined by socioeconomic traits; fertility is not an outcome.

title: No Partner, No Children? Union Formation, Assortative Mating, and Educational Inequalities in Fertility in Germany
design_or_role: mediation analysis of union formation and partner education
abstract_level_finding: Examines how union formation and assortative mating mediate educational differences in first- and second-birth probabilities; causal interpretation requires full-text review.
